newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber down on demand absence.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber down on demand absence.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were lower at noon on absence of demand and traders said they did not foresee an imminent rebound of the market, now facing an oversupply of raw materials.

Good weather since the start of the year has flooded the market with latex and other rubber materials and traders said stiff competition was being posed by other rubber producing centres in the region with similar problems.
"It's virtually impossible to lower Malaysian prices to the level of Indonesia and Thailand as our production and labour costs are much, much higher," said a trader.
"With this sort of scenario, it's very difficult to sell Malaysian rubber," the traded added.

At midday, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 301 cents ($1.21) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down one cent from Friday's close. February SMR 20 fell half cent to 296.50 cents.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 296 cents a kg, SMR CV at 359, SMR L at 339, SMR 10 at 297 and drum latex FOB at 235.
Traders said there might be some demand after February's Eid al-Fitr and Chinese New Year festivities, when plantations stop tapping rubber for nearly a week and put a strain on supply.
